ToStream.setOutputStreamInternal (689-735): "us-ascii" is not the literal "US-ASCII", so the writer is Encodings.getWriter -> OutputStreamWriter/StreamEncoder with REPLACE; it never sees a surrogate from text or attributes (they are always dirty, see below), only from comments.

ToStream.outputCharacters (1424-1525) and ToStream.writeAttrString (2030-2063): every char >= 127 is dirty because escapingNotNeeded (912-927) asks the us-ascii EncodingInfo; dirty chars go to accumDefaultEscape (via processDirty for text). Text: '\n' is written by processDirty without accumDefaultEscape; CR and C0/C1 controls are dirty. Attributes: TAB/LF/CR are special attribute chars with no entity string (CharInfo 190-201, 356), so they reach accumDefaultEscape.
ToStream.accumDefaultEntity (1021-1056): '&', '<', '>' (and '"' in attributes) have entity strings and return i+1, skipping the surrogate check.

ToStream.accumDefaultEscape (1693-1781) with the field m_highSurrogate (line 200), which persists across characters() and writeAttrString calls: (a) pending high != 0 and the next checked char is not a low unit -> throwIOE(high, ch) 'Invalid UTF-16 surrogate detected: <high> <ch> ?' (lines 1711-1714, 1807-1812); a low unit joins it and writeCharRef(high, low) writes &#cp; (1715-1717); (b) a high unit with i + 1 >= len (last char of the text node or attribute value) is saved in m_highSurrogate and advanced over without output (1721-1726); (c) a high unit followed in the same chunk by any non-low char -> throwIOE(high, next) (1728-1734); (d) any other surrogate, i.e. a lone low unit, fails XMLChar.isInvalid -> SAXException 'An invalid XML character (Unicode: 0x<unit>) was found in the node's character data content.' (1747-1751; the same key for attribute values). Nothing flushes m_highSurrogate at endDocument, so a pending high unit with no later checked char is dropped.
ToStream.comment (2275-2330): comment chars are written raw to the StreamEncoder, which replaces an unmappable or malformed unit with '?'. Comments never touch m_highSurrogate.

causal_divergence: The outcome is a property of ToStream's character state over the whole serialized document (text nodes and attribute values in document order), not of the preprocessed line. Rust decided at TIM projection time, so a high unit that ends a text node (Java: silently dropped) became an error, and a unit on a line that never reaches SVG became an error too.
invariant: An unpaired unit is carried from TIM projection to SVG export unchanged. Export runs ToStream's rule over the finished document in Java's node order (text nodes and attribute values in document order, attributes of one element sorted by name): checked chars are those that reach accumDefaultEscape's surrogate check; a lone low unit fails with the invalid-character message; a high unit followed in its own node by any char fails with the surrogate message unless that char is the matching low unit; a high unit that ends its node is held and either joins a low unit that is the next checked char, fails on any other next checked char, or is dropped at end of document. Comments write '?' for the unit. Any failure is a structured error and a nonzero CLI exit (T14.20); TIM and parser errors keep precedence because they occur before rendering.
representation: Rust String cannot hold an unpaired unit. A new rustuml-parser module java_utf16 maps unit u (0xD800..=0xDFFF) to the scalar U+10F800 + (u - 0xD800), the last 2048 code points of Supplementary Private Use Area-B (unassigned by Unicode), and back. Value::to_display, utf16_units, %strlen/%size and the uml_source seed hash go through it, so TIM sees exactly Java's UTF-16 units; projected lines are re-normalized so an adjacent high and low unit become the real scalar, as Java's concatenated String would. A user literal in U+10F800..U+10FFFF is therefore read as an unpaired unit: declared residue (the parent's probe rule already excludes PUA input).
width: AW surrogate_high_class gives Java textLength 22.5859 at size 14 plain for 'x' + a lone high unit; 'x' is 8.5859375 in CHAR_WIDTHS_14, so the unit advances exactly one em (14). Rust measured the lossy U+FFFD with its em fallback and matched (previous tip DIFF 1, text only). The draft measures the carrier scalar with an explicit one-em rule cited to that datum; other sizes and bold are relayed as probes, not assumed.
